sections.heading: SEO and AI search in Irvine
sections.body_html:
Irvine is a planned city in central Orange County with 307,670 residents in the 2020 census. Several major technology and semiconductor companies have headquarters there, and the city has been rated one of the top cities for start-ups.

It is also home to the University of California, Irvine and other higher-education campuses, with commercial districts including the Irvine Business Complex near John Wayne Airport and Irvine Spectrum to the east.

sections.heading: How Irvine customers search
sections.body_html:
That makes Irvine unusual: alongside everyday consumer searches, there is a lot of business-to-business search, from accountants and lawyers to IT and marketing services. Professional buyers often research with AI assistants before contacting anyone.

Consumer searches reflect a large residential population in planned villages, so services such as healthcare, fitness, tutoring, childcare and home services are in steady demand.

sections.heading: How Google ranks local results in Irvine
sections.body_html:
Google is unusually direct about local rankings. Its Business Profile help says local results are mainly based on relevance, distance and popularity. It describes prominence as how well-known a business is, based partly on how many websites link to it and how many reviews it has, and says more reviews and positive ratings can help. The same page adds that there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking.

Irvine's planned villages and separate business districts mean distance can shift results noticeably within the city. A business near Irvine Spectrum and one in the Irvine Business Complex compete in different local results.

sections.heading: Getting recommended by ChatGPT and Google AI in Irvine
sections.body_html:
For B2B services in Irvine, AI assistants favor firms with clear specialties, case studies, named experts and consistent information. For consumer services, clear service pages and reviews matter most.

Ask these questions in ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google each month and record who is named:

  1. Which accounting firm in Irvine works with startups?
  2. Who is the best physical therapist in Irvine?
  3. What is a good daycare in Irvine?
  4. Which IT services company in Irvine supports small businesses?
  5. Who is a good interior designer in Irvine?

sections.heading: Business Profile basics
sections.body_html:
Your Google Business Profile is usually the first thing people see in a local search.

Google's guidelines say service-area businesses, which serve customers at their locations, should have one profile for the central office or location with a designated service area. A rented mailing address you do not operate from, a virtual office, is not eligible, and P.O. boxes are not acceptable. Your business name should be your real-world name as used on your storefront, website and stationery, without extra keywords.

sections.heading: Reviews
sections.body_html:
Ask clients and customers for reviews that describe the service and outcome. B2B firms should also publish case studies with permission.

Google's Maps content policy prohibits fake engagement: reviews must reflect a genuine experience, and businesses may not offer incentives, such as payment, discounts or free services, in exchange for a review or for removing a negative one. Ask every real customer, make it easy with a direct link, and reply to reviews.

sections.heading: Structured data
sections.body_html: Add LocalBusiness structured data, or the most specific Schema.org type for your business, with your real name, address, phone, hours and service area, matching your Business Profile exactly. Google's local business documentation explains how this markup can help it show your details.

sections.heading: City pages that help Irvine customers
sections.body_html:
A page for Irvine makes sense if you serve the city's businesses or villages in a specific way, such as on-site service for offices in the business districts.

Google's spam policies list pages targeted at specific cities that funnel visitors to one page, and substantially similar pages, as doorway abuse. Create a city page only when you have something specific to say about work there, such as local projects, permits or response times, and link it clearly from your main service pages.
